skill.name: hugging-face-jobs
skill.description: Submit and manage Hugging Face Jobs for ML workloads with hardware selection, secure tokens, and result persistence.
skill.summary: Run managed ML workloads on Hugging Face Jobs with practical guidance for secrets, hardware, and saved outputs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation and helper scripts for Hugging Face Jobs. Most static findings are Markdown or example-code false positives, but several real medium-risk issues remain around unpinned remote script execution and shell examples that expose HF_TOKEN handling. No prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Insecure token exposure in shell examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace HF_TOKEN shell command substitution examples with Hugging Face secret flags or MCP secrets, and avoid putting token values in shell history or process arguments.
Prefer bundled scripts, inline reviewed code, or pinned commit URLs before passing secrets to jobs that execute remote scripts.

remediation.issue: Credential access in runnable helper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Keep HF_TOKEN scoped to required Hub operations, avoid logging token values, and document the minimal token permissions for each script.

content.value_statement: Managed ML jobs require careful setup for hardware, secrets, timeouts, and result persistence. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to submit Hugging Face Jobs with secure tokens and repeatable scripts.
actual_capabilities: Creates hf_jobs MCP submissions for UV scripts and Docker jobs.
Selects CPU, GPU, and TPU flavors based on workload size.
Explains HF_TOKEN secret handling for Hub reads and uploads.
Guides result persistence to Hugging Face Hub, S3, GCS, or APIs.
Uses included scripts for vLLM responses, CoT self-instruct data, and FinePDFs statistics.
Covers scheduled jobs, logs, cancellation, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires a Hugging Face account with Jobs access and available quota.
Does not verify third-party remote script URLs or model behavior.
Cloud jobs can incur costs if hardware and timeouts are oversized.
Included scripts may need user-specific dataset, model, and token permissions.

use_cases.title: Run Batch Inference
use_cases.description: Generate responses for a Hub dataset with vLLM and push outputs to a dataset repository.

use_cases.title: Process Large Datasets
use_cases.description: Run CPU or GPU data processing jobs without local hardware and persist results to the Hub.

use_cases.title: Schedule Recurring Jobs
use_cases.description: Create scheduled jobs for reports, tests, or repository event workflows with clear monitoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hugging-face-jobs to run a small CPU test job. Use a 10 minute timeout and do not persist results.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Dataset Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hugging-face-jobs to run batch inference on my Hub dataset. Recommend hardware, timeout, token needs, and where outputs should be saved.

prompt_templates.title: Persist Training Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Hugging Face Jobs plan that trains or processes data and pushes artifacts to my Hub repository using HF_TOKEN secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scheduled Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scheduled Hugging Face Jobs workflow for a weekly dataset report. Include schedule, hardware, secrets, monitoring, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Run batch inference for a prompt dataset and save responses.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a job plan with recommended GPU flavor, timeout, token requirements, persistence target, and monitoring details.

output_examples.input: Analyze a large Hub dataset without downloading it locally.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a streaming data job, explains the expected cost controls, and describes the Hub dataset that will store results.
The assistant outlines the schedule, secret requirements, status checks, cancellation path, and storage location for each run.

best_practices: Use secrets for HF_TOKEN and keep token permissions minimal.
Start with small hardware and short samples before scaling.
Persist results before the job exits, preferably to the Hub.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding Hugging Face tokens in prompts, scripts, or job logs.
Running unpinned remote scripts from unfamiliar repositories.
Submitting long jobs without timeout, cost, and persistence checks.

faq.question: Does this skill run jobs locally?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and submits Hugging Face Jobs that run on managed Hugging Face infrastructure.

faq.question: When is HF_TOKEN required?
faq.answer: HF_TOKEN is required for private Hub access, uploads, repository creation, and other authenticated Hub operations.

faq.question: Can it use GPUs?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps choose available CPU, GPU, and TPU flavors based on workload needs.

faq.question: Does it save results automatically?
faq.answer: No. The job script must push results to Hub or another storage target before exit.

faq.question: Is it safe to use remote script URLs?
faq.answer: Use pinned and trusted URLs only. Prefer bundled scripts or inline code when secrets are passed.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that support the required Hugging Face tools.
